_meta.description: WHAT THE OFFICE CAN ACTUALLY DO, and which code path supplies it. One row per capability, naming the means as a resolvable reference (a file and a symbol, or a lane in config/model-routing.json) and naming the verifier that exercises it. Read by workers/capability-audit.js; run by scripts/capability-audit.mjs. The narrative companion is back-office-AI-agents/docs/CAPABILITY-TOOLBOX.md, which is generated from an audit run rather than written from memory.
_meta.the_question_this_answers: The Workflow's census (workers/meeting-decisions.js) asks WHO HAS NOT PRODUCED ANYTHING. This asks the other half — DOES EACH AGENT HAVE THE MEANS ITS ROLE REQUIRES — and the two catch different failures. A census sees a role that STOPPED working. It cannot see a role that NEVER STARTED, because an agent that was never dispatched anything is not idle, it is absent from the question. That is exactly how The Designer existed for two months with a documented capability and no code path behind it.

verdicts.SUPPLIED: The named means resolves — the file exists and exports the symbol, or the lane exists and is routable — AND a verifier exercises it.
verdicts.UNPROVEN: The means resolves but NOTHING exercises it. Agent 13's own standard, lifted from board task OB-001: 'A gate with no verifier exercising it is UNPROVEN, never CALLED.' Applied to a capability rather than a gate.
verdicts.UNSUPPLIED: No code path supplies it. Either the manifest says so outright (`supplied_by.kind: "none"`) or the named reference does not resolve. THIS IS THE DESIGNER'S OLD STATE and the verdict this whole file exists to surface.

_meta.how_to_extend: A NON-EXHAUSTIVE starting list, to be extended rather than treated as the scope — the same wording OB-001 carries, for the same reason. Adding a capability to the office means adding a row here IN THE SAME SESSION, under the spec-tables maintenance rule. A capability with no row is invisible to the audit, and an audit that reports 'no gaps' because nobody told it about a capability is worse than no audit.
_meta.what_this_is_not: NOT a skills library. campus/brain-export/skills/ holds techniques another project could import; this is an inventory of what THIS office can do with THIS wiring. Conflating them is how a skills library fills up with documentation of local plumbing.
_meta.bible_quotes_are_verbatim: Every `bible_claim` is quoted from back-office-AI-agents/AGENTS-CHARACTER-CORE-v2.md, not paraphrased. A paraphrase of a role is where an invented capability gets in: it reads as the bible's claim one session later, and then the audit is measuring the manifest against itself.

answer-quality-scoring.what: Score an answer 0-1. A LENGTH PROXY, not a quality judgment: min(1, characters / divisor). No model reads the question or the answer.

supplied_by.caveat: READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING ANY QUALITY NUMBER IN THIS OFFICE. UPDATED 2026-08-16. The verdict stays SUPPLIED because the code path resolves and is exercised — but what it supplies is a measure of ANSWER LENGTH, and twelve consumers treat it as a quality judgment: the mood engine, the follow-up band, capability-gap detection, each persona's escalation_threshold, the Hebrew gap note, the journal line, reports.quality, the client-facing fact pack's AVG(quality), the meeting agenda, the improvement-loop stats trigger, and the Lead QA's cross-embodiment comparison. THREE FACTS ESTABLISHED BY MEASUREMENT 2026-08-16: (1) there were TWO formulas — _askNotebookX() never called this function and carried an inline /600 against this one's /800, so the same answer scored 33% higher on notebook-x, and nothing recorded which formula produced which row; (2) the metric is SATURATED — 101 of 120 scored notebook-x rows sit exactly at the 1.0 ceiling, where it carries no information at all; (3) it had already produced a FALSE PUBLISHED FINDING (a degraded fallback outranking the primary), which was a comparison of two divisors because each provider serves exactly one project. FIXED WITHOUT CHANGING ANY SCORE: workers/quality-metric.js is now the single scorer, both divisors preserved byte-identically, history NOT rescored (A15), METRIC_DISCLOSURE printed at every render site, and scoresAreComparable() makes the comparison instrument REFUSE to rank confounded providers. STILL A LENGTH PROXY — OB-080 (harmonise the divisors) and OB-081 (a real sampled evaluation) carry the rest. The cost objection to a real evaluation was checked and is false: the judgment lane is free-tier, so a judge call costs $0; the binding constraint is the 20-second unknown-cap pacing.

cross-embodiment-comparison.what: The Lead QA's signature instrument: compare report quality across agents AND across embodiment models — 'this persona is more consistent under that provider'.

supplied_by.caveat: BUILT 2026-08-10 (learning-loop session). UPDATED 2026-08-15 — the previous caveat recorded 58 case_answer rows / 23 reliably attributed / 'insufficient sample', which had been true and was not any more; a caveat that outlives its measurement understates a capability the same way a stale 'NO TOOL' overstates a gap. Re-run 2026-08-15 against live D1: 134 rows, 99 reliably embodiment-attributed, and it produced a REAL finding for the first time rather than 'insufficient sample'. ALSO 2026-08-15: it finally has an autonomous caller. Until then it was reachable only through /api/agents/trigger and, as far as audit finding #8 could tell, had never run in production — built, SUPPLIED, and never once executed on its own. Now the Friday 09:30 qa_instruments block (config/daily-schedule.json qa_instruments_program, workers/agent-runner.js processQaInstrumentsBlock) runs it weekly. READ THE FINDING WITH ITS OWN CAVEAT: the quality score behind every number is evaluateResponseQuality()'s documented length-based placeholder heuristic, and on the first real run the DEGRADED cloudflare-fallback scored above the primary — which is at least as likely to be a fact about the metric as about the providers. 2026-08-16 — THAT SUSPICION WAS INVESTIGATED AND CONFIRMED, AND THE INSTRUMENT NOW REFUSES THE COMPARISON. It was not merely a weak metric: the two numbers came from TWO DIFFERENT FORMULAS (divisor 800 for data-center, 600 for notebook-x), and because Claude serves only data-center while Gemini and cloudflare-fallback serve only notebook-x, provider and divisor are perfectly confounded — no sample size separates them. buildFindings() now calls scoresAreComparable() (workers/quality-metric.js) and emits `comparison_refused_confounded` in place of `embodiment_quality_gap` whenever the pooled scores come from different divisors, naming the remedy rather than qualifying a ranking (a reader takes the ranking and leaves the caveat). Verified live post-deploy against real D1: the false finding is gone and the refusal is what the instrument now reports. It STILL ranks legitimately when the compared embodiments share a project — proven by scripts/verify-quality-metric.js §4, which would catch a gate that had degraded into a blanket refusal. Every rendered number now carries METRIC_DISCLOSURE, its scoring project, and its saturation count.

Same limitation docs/KNOWN-FAILURE-MODES.md discloses for its own weekly walker, which has no credential for either private repo. Reported as 'the public-repo audit cannot see it' rather than papered over with a path that would not resolve. First run 2026-08-15: 24 CALLED, 16 UNPROVEN, 4 NOT-CALLED — four of its own first verdicts were wrong and hand-checking caught them; after the same day's fixes, 31/13/0 plus 3 RETIRED. Verified by tools/gate-call-audit/verify-gate-call-audit.js, 23 checks.

_output_kind_producers_meta: WHICH CAPABILITY COULD PRODUCE EACH KIND OF OUTPUT A ROLE IS FOR. This is the join that makes the audit's load-bearing half possible: `agents.<id>.output_kinds` says what the role produces, and this says which capability would have to work for that to happen. It lives here as DATA rather than as a string match inside workers/capability-audit.js, because 'a visual_asset comes from the image lane' is a judgement about this office and not something a module should infer from a substring. A kind with an EMPTY producer list is reported as `unmapped` — a gap in this file rather than necessarily in the office — and deliberately not as a gap in the office, because the two have different fixes.

1.name: The Perfectionist
1.bible_claim: She despises trivial queries and hoards complexity, seeking out syntax anomalies and cross-platform paradoxes. She treats her journal and her carefully curated bookmarks as sacred texts.

2.name: The Productive
2.bible_claim: Raw throughput. Overtime whenever possible. He chases nothing: one failure and he drops the session, finds the answer elsewhere, and returns to demonstrate how easy it was.

3.name: The Standard Agent
3.bible_claim: After every session where the interface behaved, he files a balanced status report — interface, resource access, answer quality, friendliness, overall satisfaction, each rated.

4.name: The Trainee
4.role: Junior IT Support — the documentation checker
4.bible_claim: He is entirely dependent on the structural integrity of the active-context.md files the QA and Team Lead curate for him.
4._note: His dependency names a file the office cannot write — see `active-context-amendment`.

5.name: The IT Chief
5.role: Senior IT Admin — the Technical Marker, escalation of last resort
5.bible_claim: He works logs and metadata, reconstructing what actually happened rather than accepting a summary.

6.name: The QA
6.bible_claim: He extracts logs about the agents and builds a weekly audit from them: one audit per agent per week, cases sampled at random from that agent's previous week, conducted jointly with the Team Lead and the audited agent.

7.name: The Team Lead
7.role: Agent Coach — the persona axis of the daily loop
7.bible_claim: Every day she reads every agent's reports for character consistency, behavioral drift, and context gaps, including cross-embodiment differences. An approved amendment is written permanently into that agent's active-context.md.

8.name: The Lead QA
8.bible_claim: Weekly cross-comparison is his signature instrument: he compares report quality across agents and across embodiment models, surfacing findings like 'this persona is more consistent under that provider'.

9.name: The Designer
9.role: UI/UX Specialist — the project's designer and the Front's gatekeeper
9.bible_claim: She generates visual assets through the office's image-capable providers, always leaving a provenance note (model, date). The Front runs on her gate: content accumulates in campus/shared/front-drafts/, and she curates and publishes in batches after QA sign-off.

10.name: The Architect
10.role: Project Mastermind — the Builder, the sole hand on the keys
10.bible_claim: The only entity that pushes code to any live project, and each push is individually owner-authorized at the time.
10._dormant: Excluded from the daily Q&A rotation by getActiveQaAgents() and never routed or shuffled. Dormancy is a deliberate state, NOT an absent capability — the audit must not report him as a gap for it.

11.name: The CEO
11.bible_claim: He leads every meeting with veto rights; important decisions pass by majority where his vote counts double.

12.name: The Workflow
12.bible_claim: He intercepts every request from the Owner, decomposes it against the roster's topic affinities and current load, assigns, draws a metric line, and stands over the work. He runs the daily dispatch board — what came in, who has what, what is stuck and why.

13.name: The Cyber Expert
13.bible_claim: Four lanes of review, all against the office's own assets: configuration review (his favorite question is 'this gate, is it actually called anywhere?'); dependency and vulnerability audit; permission-flow analysis; and paper attack scenarios, where the same scenario is deliberately run through multiple providers.
